releases.name: v0.3.0
releases.intro: Reminders reach students where they are: e-mail from chalkback.xyz, Telegram with a one-tap connect link, and free push notifications. Plus this week's security updates and server tools.

Security: Pillow 12.3 → 13.0 (24 CVEs; it decodes uploaded board images) and certifi 2026.10.19.
Deploys pull fresh base images, so fixes such as Node.js 22.23.4 (October 2026 security release, CVE-2026-111497 and others) reach the web build. Previously cached images were reused.
GitHub Actions are pinned to commit SHAs instead of movable tags.
Reminders for the public demo teacher's students are logged as skipped and never delivered, so the demo login cannot be used to send e-mail or Telegram messages to anyone.
Fixed: The app's caching on the live site: fingerprinted assets are cached for a year, everything else is revalidated, and missing files are 404 instead of the app page (Cloudflare had cached the page in place of the…
Added: Push notifications (Web Push) as a free reminder channel: students turn them on per device; works on Android, desktop, and iPhone from the home screen. Migration 0003.
Telegram connect links. Teachers (or students themselves) get a one-time t.me/<bot>?start=<code> link; pressing Start connects the student's Telegram for reminders.
Icons at every size from the existing logo (branding/): Telegram bot picture, iPhone and Android home-screen icons, .ico fallback, and a web app manifest for the app.

python -m app.cli: server-side account commands for production, where registration is closed: list-teachers, create-teacher (confirms the address first), set-email (fix a typo), set-password, delete-teacher (only…

releases.name: v0.2.0
releases.intro: Live at https://chalkback.xyz: real lesson boards imported exactly, recaps that read them, and an Ansible-managed server with backups and migrations.

Added: Ansible provisioning and deploys (deploy/ansible). One playbook hardens a fresh Ubuntu server (key-only SSH, ufw, fail2ban, unattended upgrades, swap), installs Docker, and ships main with git archive, so only…
Database migrations (Alembic). The app upgrades its schema at startup; existing databases are stamped as the baseline and keep their data.
Nightly backups of the database and uploads on the server (Ansible role backup, 14 days), with restore steps in the deployment docs.
Entity-relationship diagrams are recognized and explained as data models, not algorithms.
Recap section titles (and reminder e-mail subject and button) follow the recap's language.
Exact draw.io import. HTML exports, .drawio and .xml files become boards immediately, with no AI and no cost.
Board vocabulary for real lessons. Sticky notes and note grids, code blocks, frames, picture regions, and connectors attached to elements, for both draw.io and AI-reconstructed boards.
A fictional draw.io demo lesson ("Linked lists") in the seed data.
Running the production Docker stack locally (deploy/local.env).
Changed: draw.io fidelity. Table cells keep their fill colors and headers (red/green filtering steps on database boards).
Recaps say so honestly when a board is thin or partial, and read red/green table marks.
Serbian recaps are always written in Cyrillic, and new students default to Serbian.

Recaps understand flowcharts. Boards' flowcharts are read as algorithms: START/INPUT/ OUTPUT, IF and REPEAT with branch labels (including T/F written next to arrows), boxed or joined shapes as units, called boxes as…
Board reconstruction sends its vocabulary as a validated tool schema instead of structured outputs, which rejected it as too large. It streams, with room for dense boards.
AI-read text, sticker and shape labels are sized to fit what they cover.
The AI reconstruction prompt and schema target the real board material: Miro screenshots of programming, math, electronics and database lessons, often stitched into collages.
Deploy and AI review workflows stay off until DEPLOY_ENABLED / AI_REVIEW_ENABLED are set.

releases.name: v0.1.0
releases.intro: First release: the full loop from whiteboard photo to student reminder, running end to end in mock-AI mode.

Added: API (FastAPI): teacher and student accounts with JWT auth, students, lessons, boards, reminder log. SQLite for development, PostgreSQL in production.
Board reconstruction: image and PDF uploads (one board per page) are rebuilt by Claude vision into a validated scene of text, LaTeX math, shapes, arrows and strokes.
Lesson recaps: per-student summaries (topics, key points, formulas, exercises, practice) in the student's language.
Reminders: Telegram and email (Resend) delivery, an idempotent scheduler before each student's next lesson, and a "send now" action.
Web app (React + tldraw): teacher and student dashboards, editable boards over the original photo, a custom KaTeX math shape, autosave, and a recap panel.
Mock mode: deterministic AI output when no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set.
Landing page with an animated reconstruction hero and an "autopilot" timeline generated from git history.
Documentation site (MkDocs Material).
Deployment: Docker Compose with Caddy (HTTPS) and Postgres, a Hetzner bootstrap script, and GitHub Actions for CI, AI PR review, releases and deploys.
